Chapter 11: Freedom from Time—Beyond Past and Future.
You know, time is such a practical tool in our lives... but for a lot of us, it ends up causing real pain. Our minds are always bouncing back and forth—rehashing old memories, or worrying about what’s next—and we almost never get a break in the present moment. This constant tug-of-war creates a sense that we’re always running behind, never quite catching up, always feeling like there’s not enough time. Think about someone who’s haunted by regrets. They might spend hours replaying their mistakes, wishing things had turned out differently. Or maybe you know someone who lies awake at night, anxious about what the future holds... their mind racing with “what ifs” and worries. In both cases, life isn’t really happening in the here and now—it’s somewhere else entirely.
But what if you could have a new relationship with time? It’s not about pretending the past never happened, or refusing to plan ahead. It’s about realizing that the only place you can actually live your life... is right now. The past? It’s just a memory. The future? Simply a projection. Both of them only exist inside your mind.
So, what do you do if you’re struggling with guilt or regret? The practice is gentle: notice when your mind drifts back to what’s already happened, and bring your attention to what you can sense right now. Over time, the heavy feeling of regret starts to lift, replaced by a sense of possibility in the present. And if you’re feeling anxious, overwhelmed by what’s coming next, the same approach applies—return again and again to your breath, your body, the world around you as it is in this moment.
Now, freedom from time doesn’t mean ignoring your responsibilities, or refusing to make plans. It’s about acting from a place of presence, rather than being pushed around by fear or longing. It’s letting go of that old belief that happiness is always somewhere else—waiting for you in the next big thing, the next relationship, the next moment.
Picture someone who’s been waiting ages for a promotion. One day, they realize: life is happening right now—not off in some distant, imagined future. Suddenly, that anxious waiting loses its power, and they start to feel gratitude for the present instead. Sure, the future will come—but when it does, it’ll always show up as now.
Most people never notice just how much of their suffering comes from living somewhere else in time. But with a little awareness, you can loosen the grip of the past and future. And what you find is a whole new kind of freedom—a freedom to live fully, to love deeply, and to be at peace with what’s right here, right now.
